title: Structured Output
motto: "Ask the model nicely to return JSON" fails 5 to 15 percent of the time, even on frontier models. Structured outputs close that gap with constrained decoding: the model is literally prevented from emitting a token that would violate the schema. OpenAI's strict mode, Anthropic's schema-typed tool use, Gemini's `responseSchema`, Pydantic AI's `output_type`, and Zod's `.parse` are five surface forms of the same idea. This lesson builds the schema validator and the strict-mode contract learners will use for every production extraction pipeline.

steps.title: Why this matters
cards: An agent reading a purchase-order email needs to turn free text into `{customer, line_items, total_usd}`. Three approaches.

**Approach one: prompt for JSON.** "Reply in JSON with fields customer, line_items, total_usd." Works 85 to 95 percent of the time on frontier models. Fails in six ways: missing brace, trailing comma, wrong types, hallucinated fields, truncated at token limit, leaked prose like "Here is your JSON:".
